⚠️ **Why this claim is being written now, on a card that carries no other comment.**

The original claim comment lived on **#19365** and went with it when that card stopped resolving on 2026-09-21. The rebuild (this card) restored the work item, the ruling and the record pointers — but ⛔ **not the protocol carriers that lived in its comment thread**, and this seat did not anticipate that at rebuild time.

It surfaced mechanically rather than by recollection: `node scripts/pm/check-clause2-carriers.mjs --pair 19493` exits **4** on **C2**, reporting 「no comment on the card's thread is a claim comment, so the carrier this limb reads does not exist」. The enqueue gate's declaration limb reads the `Clause-②:` line off the claim comment and nothing else, so without this comment PR #19493 could not enqueue however green it went.

⭐ Two disciplines the checker itself names and this comment obeys: the `Clause-②: yes` line is **copied from the template** in `SKILL.md` 〈模板与表〉 rather than composed — the checker records that every measured miss of this predicate was a line written from memory. And `Thread-read:` reads `none` because this card genuinely carried **zero** comments at the moment the claim was written, which is the template's own spelling for that case.

⛔ The declaration is unchanged from the original: `yes`. It is ⛔ not re-judged here — four at-tier contract reviews on PR #19493 have already read this diff, and the declaration is the conservative gate-trigger, ⛔ not the verdict.

## ✅ Correction — this PR is NOT blocked any more. It is **in the merge queue**.

`domain:spec` execution seat 2, session `session_01UDXER3sdqfeVYpEWZs5mZx`, 2026-09-22T00:3xZ.

The maintainer re-granted the permission and the call was retried. ⛔ **The earlier standing-down note on this PR — "`auto_merge` could not be enabled … the only remaining act is enabling auto-merge" — is now false and is retracted here.**

### ⚠️ And the seat's first read-back of that retry was WRONG. Recording it, because it is the more useful half.

`PUT .../ccr/auto_merge` returned `200 {"enabled":true,"merge_method":"squash"}`. The seat then read `GET /pulls/{n}` and saw **`auto_merge: null`** on all four, and was one step from reporting *"returned 200 but stored nothing"* — the known 「状态码不作数」 failure shape.

**That reading was the wrong instrument.** On a repository with a merge queue, the action does not populate the `auto_merge` attribute at all — it **enqueues the PR**. The repo's own channel table says so in as many words: 「问本仓 auto-merge 是否经队列,答案来自尝试动作,不来自属性字段」, and its criterion ② is the **`added_to_merge_queue` timeline event**. The seat read the field the table warns has no discriminating power, ⛔ not the event the table names.

**The evidence, on two independent instruments:**

1. **Timeline** — `added_to_merge_queue` on all four, at 00:35:03 / 00:35:05 / 00:35:06 / 00:35:08Z, the exact moment of the four PUTs.
2. **git, zero quota** — the queue branches exist on `origin` and are **chained**, each built on the previous one's result:

```
gh-readonly-queue/main/pr-19602-1c16889a…  -> dc9e29bb
gh-readonly-queue/main/pr-19609-dc9e29bb…  -> 71f94e29
gh-readonly-queue/main/pr-19610-71f94e29…  -> 157c62f9
gh-readonly-queue/main/pr-19493-157c62f9…  -> 85265e6f
```

⇒ queue order **#19602 → #19609 → #19610 → #19493**, each tested against the cumulative result of the ones ahead of it. That is the merge queue doing its job, and it is ⛔ **not** a bypass: the seat did not merge, did not enqueue by hand, and submitted no approving review.

### What happens next

Each PR merges as its queue branch goes green. ⚠️ A queue branch can still fail — it tests a combination that never existed before — and if it does, the PR is ejected and that is this seat's to diagnose, ⛔ not a re-enqueue on reflex.

## Door ① has landed. ⛔ The card does NOT close — doors ②③ are gated. State moves `pm:dispatched` → `pm:blocked`.

`domain:spec` execution seat 2, session `session_01UDXER3sdqfeVYpEWZs5mZx`, 2026-09-22T01:3xZ.

### What changed

**PR #19493 merged at 2026-09-22T01:10:01Z** through the merge queue. That is **door ①** (`GET /api/automation/:name/runs`, letter C — `cursor` retired via `retiredKey()`, `hasMore` computed from the engine).

⛔ **The merge did not and must not close this card**, and that was deliberate on the PR's side: it is `Part of` this card, ⛔ not `Fixes`. This card's own body already says why, quoting PR #19493 verbatim: *"A merge that shut the card would strand two-thirds of the ruled work, so the card stays open and the seat re-labels it."* ⇒ this comment is that re-labelling.

### Why the state is `pm:blocked` and ⛔ not `pm:queue`

| door | subject | state now |
|:--|:--|:--|
| ① | `GET /api/automation/:name/runs` | ✅ **landed** — PR #19493, merged 01:10:01Z |
| ② | export jobs | **ruled** (letter C), ⛔ gated on a cloud-repo reading |
| ③ | AI conversations (`ai.conversations.list`) | **ruled** (letter A), ⛔ gated on the same reading |

Doors ②③ are **already ruled** — ⛔ so this is not a decision-box item and re-presenting it would be re-litigating a maintainer ruling. They are gated on a **cloud-repo reading**, which is a missing input, not a missing decision. ⇒ `pm:blocked` is the state the model prescribes: 「等上游」, with the upstream named on a machine-greppable body line.

**The gate, verified rather than recalled:** the reading rode #19361, which no longer resolves; it is rebuilt as **#19545**, which I read just now — `HTTP 200`, `open`, `domain:spec`, titled *"[reading request from domain:spec] REBUILD of #19361…"*. Lit control on the same instrument in the same act: the neighbouring **#19546 → 404**, so the 200 is a reading and not a route that answers 200 for everything.

⚠️ **And #19545 is a PLACEHOLDER, which the taker must know before treating it as a gate that will simply open.** Its own text says the original request did not survive and asks its riders to **restate the reading** rather than inventing one. ⇒ unblocking this card is not "wait for #19545 to be answered" — it is 「a rider restates what reading is needed」, and this card is one of the riders.

### What this seat is doing, and ⛔ not doing

- Labels: `pm:dispatched` → `pm:blocked`, four-step write with read-back.
- Body gains a machine-greppable `Blocked-by: #19545` line so the unlock scan finds it. ⛔ Not a new label, ⛔ not a new sweep.
- ⛔ **Not closing this card.** ⛔ Not returning it to `pm:queue` — a card whose gate is a missing reading is not dispatchable, and putting it back in the queue would hand a dev a job it cannot finish.
- ⛔ **Not restating the reading here.** That is the rider's substantive act and it wants its own round; ⛔ this seat does not invent a request text that did not survive.
- `assignee` stays: door ①'s records live on PR #19493 and this seat follows the card to its end.
